text:
Sam (oncall): incident-bot: page triggered: high 5xx and user throttles for hosted-api-prod 2109876543
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout v2-ratecap-2026-03-15 to hosted-api-prod at 2109876500 by marco
Sam (oncall): seeing spike in 429s for /v1/generate, dashboard shows sudden jump at 14:02 UTC
Priya (SRE): I can confirm — overall 429 rate up ~18% in the last 2m, errors concentrated in eu-west region
Tess (support): multiple customer tickets: "requests dropped" for org:acme-inc and org:macrohealth, customers reporting timeouts and degraded UX
Marco (eng): rolling change was a rate limiter config to tighten global token bucket for cost control — new defaults applied incorrectly (missing exemptions)
Sam (oncall): can we pause the rollout or kill the flag? Is there a kill-switch?
Marco (eng): yes, killing flag now: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/flags/rollout/v2-ratecap-2026-03-15/kill`
deploy-bot: Flag kill acknowledged, stopping rollout at 14:05:12 UTC
Priya (SRE): traffic still showing 429s but trending down. Looks like some instances still running the new config (canary partial rollback didn't fully sync)
Sam (oncall): initiating rollback of the canary to v2-ratecap-previous, can someone run `kubectl rollout undo` on the canary pool?
Marco (eng): running undo on canary pool now. Command: ```kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/ratecap-canary --to-revision=23```
Marco (eng): done, controller reports restart of 4 pods, they should pick up old config in ~30s
Priya (SRE): in the meantime I'm opening temporary quota exception for enterprise customers to stop token accounting enforcement: `rlctl grant-exemption --org acme-inc --duration 2h`
Tess (support): confirming with Acme and MacroHealth that requests are improving, will update tickets once stable
Sam (oncall): any sign of token accounting drift or double-charging? We saw token mismatch alerts during the spike
Marco (eng): yes, the new limiter changed accounting window causing some requests to be consumed twice in our metering layer — billing pipeline emitted `token_mismatch` events, I'm reverting config in metering as well
Priya (SRE): metrics: 5xxs back to baseline, 429s dropping from +18% to +2% in last 4 minutes, latency normalized for affected endpoints
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-004 - "Canary rate limiter tightened without exemptions causing customer throttles" - severity: P1 - paged SRE
Sam (oncall): Good. Let's keep page open for 30m. Marco, capture root cause steps. Priya, preserve logs and snapshot Prometheus query ranges for the window 14:00-14:10 UTC
Marco (eng): root cause draft: misread default config template — `default_exemptions_enabled: false` pushed unintentionally. Deploy process didn't validate exemption presence for enterprise org ids. Also bug in rollout controller allowed partial rollout with stale cached config on some hosts
Tess (support): Customer impact notes: ~6 enterprise customers experienced throttling, ~1200 user requests failed, tickets created: #4521 #4522 #4523. No SLA breaches yet but high risk, offered status updates and credited a week of premium for affected orgs
Sam (oncall): mitigation summary: pause rollout (flag kill), rollback canary, open temporary exemptions, revert billing metering config. All actions logged. Status: recovering
Priya (SRE): postmortem action items: 1) add pre-rollout validation that exemption list is non-empty for templates, 2) fix rollout controller cache invalidation, 3) add automatic canary health check that gates applying rate config if 429s spike >3x baseline, 4) better observability linking token accounting alerts to rollout ids
Marco (eng): I'll own #1 and #2. Priya take #3, Tess own #4 with PM for customer comms
Sam (oncall): handing off to oncall followup. If anything regresses ping me. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and initial RCA
Tess (support): sending consolidated update to affected customers now. ETA for full postmortem: 48h
incident-bot: INC-2026-03-15-004 acknowledged by Sam (oncall) at 14:18 UTC
Sam (oncall): closing real-time page at 14:25 UTC — moving to follow-up channel for postmortem notes, keep monitoring for next 2 hours
Priya (SRE): monitoring snapshot links: https://prometheus.internal/r/graph?from=1700008800&to=1700009400&expr=rate_http_429
Marco (eng): logs for deploy controller: ```2026-03-15T14:01:59Z INFO apply ratecap config template v2
2026-03-15T14:02:00Z WARN missing exemption list in template
2026-03-15T14:02:05Z INFO rollout controller: applied to subset hosts (canary)```
Tess (support): tickets updated with timeline. I'll attach customer logs to the incident ticket for postmortem
Sam (oncall): thanks team. Follow-up channel: #inc-2109876543-followup
